title: A faster vibration in one medium
misconception: wavelength doubles when frequency doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply λ = v/f to compare wavelength when frequency changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a wave travelling at fixed speed in a nondispersive medium, λ = v/f. When frequency doubles, wavelength becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model λ = v/f; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a wave travelling at fixed speed in a nondispersive medium, with a nonzero initial result. If frequency triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on wavelength?
recall.why: Apply λ = v/f under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
